History
sections.wikitext:
Produced by one of the co-writers, [[Jeff Barry]], "Sugar, Sugar" features a group of [[studio musician]]s managed by [[Don Kirshner]], former music supervisor to [[the Monkees]]. It was written in the key of [[D major]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Andy |first1=Kim |last2=Jeff |first2=Barry |last3=Archies |first3=The |date=2007-01-23|title=Sugar, Sugar |url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0055948 |access-date=2021-06-02 |website=Musicnotes.com}}</ref> [[Ron Dante]] provided the lead vocals, accompanied by [[Toni Wine]] and the other co-writer, [[Andy Kim (singer)|Andy Kim]]. Together, they provided the voices of [[the Archies]] using [[multitrack recording|multitracking]]. The single was initially released in late May 1969 on Kirshner's Calendar label (as with the group's two previous singles, "[[Bang-Shang-A-Lang]]" and "[[Feelin' So Good (S.K.O.O.B.Y.-D.O.O.)]]"), achieving moderate success in the middle of the year in several radio markets. When re-released in mid-July 1969 (with pressings also on the Kirshner label), it attained enormous success nationwide across several months.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://text.npr.org/761616330 |title=50 Years Later, The Archies' 'Sugar, Sugar' Is Still 'Really Sweet' |website=Text.npr.org |access-date=January 2, 2022}}</ref>

Upon the song's initial release, Kirshner had promotion men play it for radio station personnel without revealing the group's name, as their previous single, "Feelin' So Good (S.K.O.O.B.Y.-D.O.O.)", had peaked at No. 53 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 chart.<ref name="billboard.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100|title=Top 100 Songs {{!}} Billboard Hot 100 Chart|website=Billboard.com|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.discogs.com/The-Archies-Feelin-So-Good-SKOOBY-DOO/master/456550|title=The Archies - Feelin' So Good (S.K.O.O.B.Y-D.O.O)|website=Discogs|year=1968 |language=en|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref> In an article published in ''[[The Washington Times]]'', Dante recounts that the label was removed from the record. It was taken to a top radio station, 1260 [[KSFB|KYA]] in [[San Francisco]], where the program director was told: "Just play it! It's a mystery group."<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2017/mar/26/sugar-sugar-singer-ron-dante-discusses-archies-ban/|title=Archies singer Ron Dante: 'Cartoon Band Man'|newspaper=[[The Washington Times]] |language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-13|first=Keith |last=Valcourt |date=March 26, 2017}}</ref>

The song was among the selections that astronaut [[Alan Bean]] chose when allowed to bring an [[audio cassette]] of music to listen to during the [[Apollo 12]] mission in November 1969. According to historian [[Andrew Chaikin]], "When it came on during the trip out from earth, the three of them <nowiki>[</nowiki>Bean, [[Pete Conrad]], and [[Richard F. Gordon Jr.|Dick Gordon]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> would hold onto the struts in the command module and bounce weightlessly to the beat, dancing their way to the moon."<ref name="Chaikin Moon">{{cite book |last1=Chaikin |first1=Andrew |title=[[A Man on the Moon]] |date=1994 |publisher=Penguin Putnam |isbn=0140272011|page=254}}</ref>
sections.text:
Produced by one of the co-writers, Jeff Barry, "Sugar, Sugar" features a group of studio musicians managed by Don Kirshner, former music supervisor to the Monkees. It was written in the key of D major. Ron Dante provided the lead vocals, accompanied by Toni Wine and the other co-writer, Andy Kim. Together, they provided the voices of the Archies using multitracking. The single was initially released in late May 1969 on Kirshner's Calendar label (as with the group's two previous singles, "Bang-Shang-A-Lang" and "Feelin' So Good (S.K.O.O.B.Y.-D.O.O.)"), achieving moderate success in the middle of the year in several radio markets. When re-released in mid-July 1969 (with pressings also on the Kirshner label), it attained enormous success nationwide across several months.

Upon the song's initial release, Kirshner had promotion men play it for radio station personnel without revealing the group's name, as their previous single, "Feelin' So Good (S.K.O.O.B.Y.-D.O.O.)", had peaked at No. 53 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. In an article published in The Washington Times, Dante recounts that the label was removed from the record. It was taken to a top radio station, 1260 KYA in San Francisco, where the program director was told: "Just play it! It's a mystery group."

The song was among the selections that astronaut Alan Bean chose when allowed to bring an audio cassette of music to listen to during the Apollo 12 mission in November 1969. According to historian Andrew Chaikin, "When it came on during the trip out from earth, the three of them <nowiki>[</nowiki>Bean, Pete Conrad, and Dick Gordon<nowiki>]</nowiki> would hold onto the struts in the command module and bounce weightlessly to the beat, dancing their way to the moon."

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
In the issue of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine dated September 20, the single started a four-week run at number one on the Hot 100, replacing [[the Rolling Stones]]' "[[Honky Tonk Women]]". It spent a then-lengthy 22 weeks on the Hot 100 (longer than any other single in 1969), and was one of only ten singles to spend 12 weeks in the Top Ten during the decade. It topped ''Billboard''{{'s}} year-end list of [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1969|the Top Hot 100 Singles of 1969]]. In August 1969 the record was certified gold by the [[RIAA certification|RIAA]] for sales of one million.{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH |title=Gold & Platinum: Searchable database |publisher=[[Recording Industry Association of America]] |access-date=November 12, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070626050454/http://www.riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?table=SEARCH |archive-date=June 26, 2007 }}
Search ''Artist: Archies'' (In 1989 the gold threshold was lowered to 500,000.){{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1989-05-14-fi-188-story.html|title=New Golden Rule: 500,000 Sales Mark for All Singles |last=Grein |first=Paul |date=May 14, 1989 |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=November 12, 2010}} In 2018 "Sugar, Sugar" ranked 81 in ''Billboard''{{Apostrophe}}s Hot 100 60th Anniversary chart.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100-60th-anniversary |title=HOT 100 60TH ANNIVERSARY |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=September 30, 2019}} Between late October and mid-December 1969 the single spent eight weeks at the top of the [[UK Singles Chart]]. "Sugar, Sugar" was awarded a gold disc in January 1970.{{cite book |title=Million selling records from the 1900s to the 1980s: an illustrated directory |url=https://openlibrary.org/works/OL120558W/Million_selling_records_from_the_1900s_to_the_1980s |first=Joseph |last=Murrells |year=1985 |publisher=Arco Pub. |isbn=0668064595 |quote=In Britain the disc (RCA label) was No 1 for eight weeks and sold over a million there |page=276}} In July 2026 the song was certified Platinum by the BPI for selling 600,000 units since it was made available digitally in November 2004. In the chart dated September 13, 1969, "Sugar, Sugar" topped the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM 100]]'' national singles chart in Canada, where it remained for three weeks. It also peaked at number one on the South African Singles Chart.{{cite web|author=Brian Currin |url=http://www.rock.co.za/files/springbok_top_20_(A).html |title=South African Singles Chart |publisher=Rock.co.za |access-date=December 27, 2010}} On February 5, 2006, "Sugar, Sugar" was inducted into the [[Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame]], as co-writer Andy Kim is originally from [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cshf.ca/fr/song/sugar-sugar/|title=Sugar Sugar|website=Cshf.ca|access-date=January 2, 2022}}
sections.text:
In the issue of Billboard magazine dated September 20, the single started a four-week run at number one on the Hot 100, replacing the Rolling Stones' "Honky Tonk Women". It spent a then-lengthy 22 weeks on the Hot 100 (longer than any other single in 1969), and was one of only ten singles to spend 12 weeks in the Top Ten during the decade. It topped Billboard{{'s}} year-end list of the Top Hot 100 Singles of 1969. In August 1969 the record was certified gold by the RIAA for sales of one million. (In 1989 the gold threshold was lowered to 500,000.) In 2018 "Sugar, Sugar" ranked 81 in Billboard{{Apostrophe}}s Hot 100 60th Anniversary chart.

Between late October and mid-December 1969 the single spent eight weeks at the top of the UK Singles Chart. "Sugar, Sugar" was awarded a gold disc in January 1970. In July 2026 the song was certified Platinum by the BPI for selling 600,000 units since it was made available digitally in November 2004.

In the chart dated September 13, 1969, "Sugar, Sugar" topped the RPM 100 national singles chart in Canada, where it remained for three weeks. It also peaked at number one on the South African Singles Chart. On February 5, 2006, "Sugar, Sugar" was inducted into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame, as co-writer Andy Kim is originally from Montreal, Quebec.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: In May 1970, [[Wilson Pickett]]'s cover of "Sugar, Sugar" reached No. 4 on ''Billboard'''s [[R&B chart]], then in June peaked at No. 25 on the Hot 100. The parent album, ''[[Right On (Wilson Pickett album)|Right On]]'', reached No. 197 on the [[Billboard 200]] album chart. Pickett's recording was used in [[Ang Lee]]'s 1997 film ''[[The Ice Storm (film)|The Ice Storm]]''. In Canada, "[[Abraham, Martin and John|Cole, Cooke & Redding]]" was the A-side and charted first, reaching No. 58 in April 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/obj/028020/f2/nlc008388.3796.pdf| title=RPM Top 100 Singles - April 25, 2970}}</ref>

sections.heading: Other versions
sections.wikitext:
* Sakkarin (a pseudonym of [[Jonathan King]]) recorded the song (as "Sugar Sugar") in 1971, reaching No. 12 in the UK chart<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/14284/sakkarin/ |title=Sakkarin |work=The Official Charts Company }}</ref> as well as No. 20 in Ireland<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.irma.ie/?s=Sakkarin |title=Sakkarin |work=The Irish Charts}}</ref> and No. 21 in Germany.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.offiziellecharts.de/titel-details-195098 |title=Sakkarin: Sugar Sugar |work=Offizielle Deutsche Charts }}</ref>
* [[Ron Dante]], lead singer of [[the Archies]], recorded a disco version of the song in 1975.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spectropop.com/RonDante/|title=Ron Dante|website=Spectropop.com|access-date=21 December 2018}}</ref>
* [[Josie and the Pussycats (comics)|Josie and the Pussycats]], another [[Archie Comics]] creation, covered the song (as "Candy Girl (Sugar Sugar)") in the first season of the TV series ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/riverdale-season-1-original-television-soundtrack/1234693908 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301044557/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/riverdale-season-1-original-television-soundtrack/1234693908 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 1, 2018 |title=Riverdale: Season 1 (Original Television Soundtrack) |date=May 12, 2017 |publisher=iTunes}}</ref>

* Josie and the Pussycats, another Archie Comics creation, covered the song (as "Candy Girl (Sugar Sugar)") in the first season of the TV series Riverdale.
